chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Abu Hanifah: 'O Abu Hanifah, what do you say about a house that collapsed on a group of people, and two children remained from them, one free and the other a slave to his master, and the free one was not distinguished from the slave?' Abu Hanifah said: 'Half of this one is freed, and half of this one is freed, and the wealth is divided between them.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Not so, but a lot is cast between them, and whoever the lot falls on is the free one, and this one is freed, so he becomes his mawla (client/freedman).'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Abu Hanifah's and Imam al-Sadiq's ruling on indistinguishable free and slave children?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration highlights the jurisprudential divergence between the emerging Sunni school of Abu Hanifah and the Imami tradition regarding *qur'ah* (lottery) as a mechanism for resolving uncertainty in inheritance and manumission. While Abu Hanifah opts for a probabilistic 'half-free' status, Imam al-Sadiq emphasizes the definitive resolution of status through lottery, ensuring the remaining child is elevated to a freedman (*mawla*) of the identified free child, thereby clarifying lineage and social standing.
